publicQuestions.question:
Neutral-to-earth link inside the generators

Reference: Drawing 2685-ELEC-1 rev0, Note; Specification clauses 2.4(b), 2.4(e) and 2.8(b).

The drawing note asks for the neutral-to-earth link to be removed inside the generator, because the site switchboard has its own link. This is correct when the generator feeds a switchboard. However, clause 2.4(b) also asks for 240 V outlets on the generator, and clauses 2.4(e) and 2.8(b) ask for earth fault and RCD protection. If the link is removed permanently, the RCDs and earth fault protection on the generator's own outlets will not work safely when the generator is used on its own, for example running tools or lighting at a site with no switchboard.

Which of the following does council want?

a) A switchable or removable link, removed when connected to a switchboard and fitted when the generator is used on its own, with an instruction label in the canopy.

b) The link permanently removed, with the generator used only through a switchboard and its own outlets used only while connected.

c) Another arrangement (please describe).
publicQuestions.answer: Council's preference would be option A

publicQuestions.question:
Trailer towing details

Reference: Specification clauses 1.4, 2.10 and 2.11.

Clause 2.10 asks for a road-registrable, hot-dip galvanised trailer, but does not state the coupling, brake type or a weight limit. The large generator with its 800 litre tank full will need a trailer rated at roughly 3.5 tonnes or more loaded (Aggregate Trailer Mass). Under the Australian Design Rules, any trailer over 2 tonnes must have brakes on every wheel and a breakaway system, so the tow vehicle needs a brake controller.

a) What coupling will council's tow vehicles use: a 50 mm tow ball, a 70 mm tow ball, or a pintle (ring and hook)? If a ball, is a heavy-duty off-road coupling preferred?

b) What is the towing capacity and tow-ball limit of the vehicles that will tow the large generator, and is there a maximum loaded trailer weight council can accept?

c) Are electric brakes acceptable, or does council require electric-over-hydraulic or another type? Do council's vehicles have brake controllers fitted?
publicQuestions.answer:
All Balonne Shire Council towing vehicles have electric brake controllers fitted. Trailer load rating 3.5 tonnes will require electric brakes on all wheels, including an automatic emergency breakaway system. Dual safety chains stamped with a capacity rating that matches or exceeds the 3,500 kg limit. The chains must be attached to the tow bar using rated D-shackles.

a) 50mm tow ball rated at 3,500 kgs or better.

b) Towing capacity not exceeding 3,500kgs, with 50 kgs tow ball limit.

c) Electric brakes are preferred.

publicQuestions.answer:
Question:

Proprietary GPT design boundary: Please confirm whether the selected GPT supplier will be responsible for the design and certification of the proprietary GPT chamber/unit, treatment internals, access covers and associated proprietary structural components, with the Consultant responsible for the site-specific civil/structural integration, foundations, pipe connections, access and surrounding works.

Answer:

The Consultant is responsible for obtaining the relevant proprietary GPT design documentation and certification from the selected manufacturer and incorporating this into the overall design.

The Consultant remains responsible for the site specific civil and structural design, foundations, pipe connections, access arrangements and integration with surrounding infrastructure.

Question:

Manufacturer certification: Please confirm whether Council requires the selected proprietary GPT supplier to provide certified design calculations/drawings for the GPT unit and chamber suitable for incorporation into the Consultant’s IFC documentation.

Answer:

The Consultant is required to provide certified Issued for Construction (IFC) drawings, incorporating relevant proprietary GPT documentation and certification obtained from the manufacturer.

Question:

Potholing provisional sum: The Pricing Schedule nominates a fixed $7,500 provisional sum for potholing. Please confirm whether this amount is to be included within the evaluated Respondent Quoted Amount / total lump sum, and whether actual potholing costs will subsequently be adjusted against the provisional sum.

Answer:

Council's $7,500 provisional sum for potholing is to be included in the Respondent's total lump sum (excluding GST). This allowance has been established based on council's officer understanding of the site and anticipated service proving requirements.

Actual potholing costs will be reconciled against the provisional sum, with any unused allowance deducted from the contract sum. Expenditure exceeding the provisional sum will require Council's prior written approval.

Question:

Extent of service proving: Please confirm Council's expected minimum potholing/service-proving scope, including the number of potholes or whether the Consultant is to determine the quantity necessary to positively locate all services potentially affected by the GPT installation.

Answer:

The Consultant is responsible for determining the appropriate geotechnical investigation scope, including the number and depth of boreholes or test pits, sufficient to assess the site's suitability for GPT installation.

This should include consideration of excavation, founding conditions, groundwater, buoyancy and shoring requirements.

Question:

Service relocation: Please confirm whether the Consultant's base scope is limited to designing the GPT arrangement to avoid existing utilities where practicable, or whether detailed design and authority coordination for relocation/protection of water, sewer, electrical, telecommunications or other utilities is also required.

Answer:

Service clashes are to be minimised and managed through design wherever practicable. Where relocation of existing services is considered unavoidable, the Consultant must advise council. Any detailed relocation design and associated authority approvals outside the agreed scope would be subject to Council's prior written approval.

Question:

Geotechnical investigation requirements: Please confirm whether Council has a prescribed minimum investigation scope, such as minimum borehole/test-pit numbers and depths, or whether the Consultant is to nominate a risk-based geotechnical investigation sufficient to assess excavation, founding conditions, groundwater, buoyancy and shoring.

Answer:

Council does not require independent hydraulic modelling of the proprietary GPT internals. The Consultant may rely on hydraulic information provided by the GPT manufacturer to inform the site-specific design and assessment of device suitability.

Question:

Contamination / ASS: Please advise whether any contamination, acid sulfate soil, fill-quality or environmental investigations are available for the site and whether these investigations form part of the Consultant's scope.

Answer:

Council has not undertaken any contamination, acid sulfate soil or other environmental investigations at the proposed location of works.

Separate contamination and acid sulfate soil investigations are not included in the base scope of the consultancy.

Should the Consultant identify potential contamination or environmental constraints during Stage 1, these are to be brought to council attention for consideration of any additional investigations.

Question:

Detailed temporary works design: The RFQ requires a construction methodology including shoring/trench-support requirements and temporary works. Please confirm whether the Consultant is required to provide the detailed certified temporary-works/shoring design, or whether the Consultant is to specify performance/design requirements with detailed temporary works to be designed and certified by the future construction contractor.

Answer:

Council will accept a performance-based approach to the temporary works design, provided the proposed construction methodology and relevant performance criteria, design requirements and constraints are clearly identified.

Question:

Stormwater diversion: Please confirm whether [Respondent] is required to fully design temporary stormwater bypass/diversion works for construction or provide only construction-stage functional requirements and indicative staging, with final temporary diversion design by the contractor.

Answer:

Construction-stage functional requirements and indicative staging, with final temporary diversion design by the contractor.

Question:

Hydraulic design boundary: The RFQ states that catchment hydraulic modelling is not required. Please confirm that Council will provide the stated 319 L/s treatable flow and 1,430 L/s peak flow as design inputs and that no independent catchment/TUFLOW/DRAINS-style verification is required from the Consultant.

Answer:

Independent catchment hydraulic modelling is not required from the Consultant. The treatable flow rate of 319 L/s and peak flow rate of 1,430 L/s provided in Schedule 1 are to be adopted as design inputs.

Question:

GPT hydraulic checks: Notwithstanding the exclusion of catchment modelling, please confirm that the Consultant is expected to review the manufacturer's hydraulic capacity/headloss/bypass information only, rather than independently hydraulically modelling the proprietary GPT internals.

Answer:

Council does not require independent hydraulic modelling of the proprietary GPT internals. The Consultant may rely on hydraulic information provided by the GPT manufacturer to assess device suitability and inform the site specific design.

Question:

Management-system certification: Clause 7 requests OHSAS18001/AS4801, ISO14001 and ISO9001 or equivalent documentation. Please confirm whether documented internal WHS, environmental and quality management systems will be accepted where a consultant is not independently certified to those standards.

Answer:

Council will accept documented internal WHS, environmental and quality management systems in lieu of third-party certification, provided they adequately demonstrate the Respondent's management arrangements.

Question:

Traffic management: Please confirm whether Stage 1 traffic-management pricing must include traffic permits, road occupancy approvals, Council fees, traffic-control plans and physical controllers/barriers, or whether any of these will be supplied/waived by Council.

Answer:

Permits, approvals and associated fees for traffic management activities are not required to be included in the Respondent's lump sum. The Consultant is required to include the costs of preparing traffic management plans and implementing the traffic control measures necessary to undertake the consultancy services, including any required controllers and barriers.

Question:

Maintenance vehicle requirements: Please provide the Council maintenance vehicle design envelope/vehicle type, axle loads, turning requirements and preferred maintenance method to be adopted in designing the GPT access area.

Answer:

Council anticipates using a vacuum excavation truck to service the GPT in accordance with the selected manufacturer's maintenance requirements.

Question:

Pre-construction dilapidation: Please confirm whether the Consultant is required to undertake the actual pre-construction dilapidation survey now, or only identify/specify the required future dilapidation survey within the construction methodology/tender documents.

Answer:

The Consultant is not required to undertake a dilapidation survey as part of this design consultancy. However, the construction methodology documents must define the scope of the pre-construction dilapidation survey to be undertaken by the future contractor.

Question:

Cost estimate accuracy: Please confirm the expected estimate classification/accuracy at 30%, 80% and IFC stages and whether an independent quantity surveyor/cost planner is required, or whether a Consultant-prepared estimate based on quantities, supplier quotations and market rates is acceptable.

Answer:

Council has not nominated a specific cost estimate classification or accuracy range for the 30%, 80% or IFC design stages.

A Consultant-prepared construction cost estimate based on quantities, supplier quotations, market rates and relevant industry knowledge is acceptable. An independent quantity surveyor or cost planner is not required.

Question:

Design reviews / comments: Please confirm that the lump sum may assume one consolidated Council comment set following each nominated 30% and 80% submission, plus one final close-out review.

Answer:

Council anticipates providing one consolidated set of comments following each nominated 30% and 80% design submission, together with a final close-out review.

Additional review cycles requested by Council involving changes outside the agreed scope may be considered as a variation. Reviews required to address errors, omissions or noncompliance with the agreed scope will not constitute a variation.

Question:

Meetings: The scope requires fortnightly Teams updates. Please confirm that these are anticipated throughout the 16-week contract period and that approximately eight fortnightly meetings, in addition to the inception/site meeting and formal 30%/80% review meetings, should be allowed.

Answer:

It is expected that council and the Consultant will meet at a minimum fortnightly. If the 30% and 80% review meetings fall within this fortnightly time frame, council would propose to have a single meeting with the Consultant.

Question:

Construction support: The RFQ notes construction-phase engineering/site inspections may subsequently be required as a variation. Please confirm no construction-phase inspections, RFIs, shop-drawing reviews or certification are to be included in the tendered lump sum.

Answer:

Council confirms that construction-phase support services, including engineering/site inspections, responses to RFIs, shop-drawing reviews and certification, are not to be included in the Respondent's tendered lump sum.

Should council require any of these services during the construction phase, they will be treated as a variation to the Consultant's engagement, subject to council's prior approval. The cost of any such variation will be negotiated based on the Consultant's submitted Schedule of Hourly Work Rates.

title: Murray Aquatic and Leisure Centre Masterplan Review, Strategy and Business Case
description:
The Shire of Murray is seeking submissions from suitably qualified multidisciplinary consultant teams to undertake a review and update of the Murray Aquatic and Leisure Centre Masterplan 2016 and prepare a contemporary, staged redevelopment and investment strategy for the future development of the Centre.

The project includes a strategic review and update of the existing Masterplan, preparation of a staged redevelopment strategy and implementation framework, operational feasibility assessment, supporting business case and investment strategy, and concept designs and preliminary construction cost estimates for prioritised Stage 1 redevelopment works.

The Murray Aquatic and Leisure Centre is located at 16 Camp Road, Pinjarra, Western Australia.

The Shire is seeking completion of the project by June 2027 where practicable, with the preferred Masterplan, staging and indicative high-level capital costs sufficiently advanced by May 2027 to support preliminary advocacy and forward planning.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Shire of Murray is a local government area of Western Australia. It has an area of 1,710.1 square kilometres (660.3 sq mi) and is located in the Peel Region about 80 kilometres (50 mi) south of the Perth central business district.

The Shire extends across the Peel Inlet and the Swan Coastal Plain into the Darling Scarp, including about 77,000 hectares (190,000 acres) of State forests. Timber logging and agriculture were the traditional enterprises of the district. However, in recent decades, bauxite mining and a significant equine and tourism industry have emerged.

The Murray River flows all year throughout the district. It offers premier country racing and trotting facilities, a golf course and an array of festivals and events.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The successful consultant will build upon the significant strategic planning, needs analysis and internal operational assessments already undertaken by the Shire. The project is not intended to recommence strategic planning and needs assessment work already completed, but rather to validate and refine this work in response to current conditions and future requirements.

A multidisciplinary and collaborative approach is required to ensure strategic planning, operational modelling, architectural planning and financial analysis collectively inform the recommended redevelopment outcomes. Relevant background documents and available operational and asset information will be provided to the successful consultant.

The preferred approach should provide practical, achievable and financially responsible solutions capable of staged implementation.

publicQuestions.question:
Proposed contract: Could the Shire please confirm the proposed consultancy agreement and provide the conditions of engagement? For example, would the WALGA terms and conditions be applicable, noting we are a WALGA panel member?

Stage 1 priorities and budget: Has the Shire identified any preferred priority Stage 1 works and an indicative capital budget to guide their scope?

Works completed since 2016: Could the Shire please confirm which (if any) recommendations or interventions from the 2016 Masterplan have since been implemented?

Asset assessment: Could the Shire please clarify the expected depth of assessment of existing buildings, plant and infrastructure? Should respondents allow for a high-level review of available asset information and previous studies, supported by a site inspection, or are detailed condition assessments / audits expected?
publicQuestions.answer:
1.	Proposed consultancy agreement and conditions of engagement (including whether WALGA terms and conditions will apply).

Note: We are running this through Public Marketplace, not WALGA panel)

The RFQ is being undertaken through Public Marketplace, rather than a WALGA Preferred Supplier Panel, and WALGA terms and conditions do not automatically apply. Consultants are invited to submit their proposed terms and conditions of engagement as part of their proposal, which will be subject to review and agreement by the Shire prior to appointment.

2.	Whether Council has identified any preferred Stage 1 priorities and/or an indicative capital budget.

Council has not formally endorsed a preferred Stage 1 scope or indicative capital budget. The Needs Analysis and draft Community Infrastructure Plan identifies priority facility needs, which this consultancy will further assess and refine through demand, operational and financial modelling to inform investment priorities, staging and the recommended Stage 1 redevelopment scope and indicative capital costs.

3.	Which recommendations from the 2016 Masterplan have been implemented to date.

The broader recommendations of the 2016 Masterplan have not been substantially implemented, although various facility improvements and asset renewal works have been undertaken. The consultancy will review the Masterplan and assess the ongoing relevance of its recommendations in developing the updated redevelopment plan.

4.	The expected level of detail for the asset assessment (high-level review versus detailed condition assessments/audits).

A high-level assessment of existing facilities, plant and equipment is expected, sufficient to identify renewal or replacement requirements for incorporation into the staged redevelopment plan and associated cost estimates.

title: MBCC500 - Building Construction Services – Preferred Supplier Arrangement
description:
City of Moreton Bay (Council) is seeking to establish a Panel Arrangement for Building Construction Services to deliver a range of minor and major projects required by Council’s Project Delivery and Facilities and Open Spaces teams.

To best align the scale and complexity of the projects with the capabilities and resources of suppliers in the market, successful suppliers will be appointed to the Panel Arrangement under a tiered structure:

Category One: delivering small to medium sized projects (up to a maximum of $1.5M (Excl GST); and/or

Category Two: delivering large and/or complex projects ($1.25m (excl GST and above).

Presently, there are 22 projects for the FY26 to FY28 period in the pipeline expected to be awarded under the Panel Arrangement, comprising of 4 Category One projects, and 18 Category Two projects.

A summary of the current project pipeline is included in Part 1 - Tender Conditions and Particulars - Annexure 1 – Project Delivery Pipeline FY26-FY28.

Types of work that may be engaged under this Panel Arrangement include, but is not limited to:

Building construction works for a range of facilities; Refurbishment and rectification projects; Site remediation associated with building projects; Demolition;

Erecting ancillary buildings and structures, including sheds, shelters, signage, park equipment associated with building projects; The design related to a construction project for Design and Construct Contracts, including obtaining all relevant approvals; External works, carparking, landscaping and infrastructure work (i.e. public utility plant) associated with the project; and Supply and installation of all fittings and fixtures associated with the Project.

These Projects will be delivered at Council facilities under a variety of site conditions, including greenfield and brownfield sites, as well as live environments. Facilities may include, but is not limited to: Sport Centres; Aquatic Centres; Theatres and Entertainment Centres; Community Centres; Depot Buildings; Office Buildings; Libraries;

Clubhouse Buildings; and Amenity Buildings.

title: Winter Harvest Festival 2027 - Marquee & Underhire Supplier
description:
Scenic Rim Regional Council is seeking quotations from suitably qualified suppliers to provide marquee and underhire services for the 2027 Winter Harvest Festival, to be held in Kalbar on Saturday 26 June 2027.

The successful supplier will provide a full-service solution including the supply, delivery, installation, furniture placement, dismantle and collection of event infrastructure across multiple festival locations. Required infrastructure includes, but is not limited to, marquees, furniture, staging, fencing, flooring, crowd control barriers, décor items and associated underhire equipment.

The festival is expected to attract approximately 5,500 attendees and operates across several locations throughout Kalbar including George Street, Kalbar Civic Centre Park, Salvation Army Grounds, School of Arts precinct and surrounding activation areas.

The contract period is anticipated to commence on 1 May 2027 and conclude on 30 July 2027. Installation will occur on 24-25 June 2027, with dismantle occurring on 26-27 June 2027.

Services must be delivered onsite in Kalbar, Queensland.

publicQuestions.question:

Additionally, for locations requiring cleaning to be completed by 7:00 am, could you please confirm the earliest permitted commencement time? Would cleaning be permitted to commence from 3:30 am or earlier if required?

publicQuestions.answer:
1.	Cleaning Times and Service Windows

Please refer to the Excel file "26 27 77 Cat A Public Toilets Cleaning Sep26", which clearly sets out the required service frequencies, cleaning times and cleaning types.

The schedule specifies:

•	Public Facility Group 1: Complete Full Clean (AM) before opening, prior to 7:00am.

•	Public Facility Group 2: Daily Full Clean and Unlock (before 8:00am), 7 days per week.

•	Public Facility Group 3: Toilets are open 24 hours and may be cleaned at any time during the day, provided the required service frequencies are achieved.

•	Where specific times are identified for additional cleans or spot cleans, these are intended to ensure facilities are inspected and maintained throughout the day, rather than relying solely on a single morning service.

2.	Timing of the Second Clean

Where a second clean is nominated for 3:00pm, the City of Ballarat would generally accept the clean being completed slightly earlier, provided the required service frequency, inspection requirements, cleanliness standards and customer outcomes are maintained.

The intent of the scheduled cleans is to ensure facilities remain hygienic, adequately serviced and fit for community use throughout the day, while minimising complaints and service issues.

3.	Earliest Permitted Commencement Time

For facilities requiring completion before opening, cleaning may generally commence up to one hour prior to the specified opening time, provided all activities are undertaken safely and in accordance with relevant operational requirements.

The facility opening, where applicable, is to occur at the times specified within the schedule.

4.	Commencement from 3:30am or Earlier

Commencement times, including 3:30am or earlier, are a matter for the Contractor's operational arrangements and service delivery approach.

The City of Ballarat’s primary requirement is that cleaning activities are completed to the required standard and that facilities are opened, unlocked and made available to the public at the times specified within the schedule. Any proposed arrangements should also take into consideration noise, safety and legislative requirements applicable to the work.

title: Application Control
description:
Queensland Treasury seeks to procure and implement an enterprise-grade Application Control solution that enables organisation-wide enforcement of the ASD Essential Eight Application Control strategy across all supported endpoint and server platforms, as well as align with the Information Security Manual (ISM).

The Customer has issued this Invitation to Offer with the objectives of achieving consistent application control enforcement across all endpoints and improved cyber resilience and compliance outcomes through sourcing a solution that will:

•	Support achievement and maintenance of ASD Essential Eight Maturity Level 2 and Level 3 requirements.

•	Provide application allowlisting and execution control.

•	Reduce operational overhead associated with policy administration.

•	Improve visibility, governance and reporting.

•	Support Windows, macOS, Linux and server operating environments.

•	Integrate with Treasury's broader endpoint security ecosystem.

•	Deliver high availability and enterprise scalability.

The proposed solution is required to be deployed, configured, tested and transitioned into operational support by 30 June 2027.

title: 201253 RFT Prince Edward Park Pedestrian Bridge Design and Construct
description:
Sutherland Shire Council invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors to tender for the Prince Edward Park Woronora Pedestrian Bridge Renewal Project.

The project involves the demolition of the existing pedestrian bridge and the construction of a new bridge to provide a safe, compliant, and durable pedestrian and cyclist crossing over the Woronora River. The works also include the construction of new shared pedestrian and bicycle path connections associated with the bridge replacement.

The existing bridge, owned by Sutherland Shire Council, provides an important active transport link between Prince Edward Park and Prices Circuit, connecting the northern and southern banks of the Woronora River. Due to the structure's age and condition, the bridge exhibits several defects and no longer meets current design and compliance requirements, affecting its safety, serviceability, and long-term performance.

The Woronora River is an environmentally sensitive area, and the successful Contractor will be required to undertake the works in accordance with all relevant environmental approvals, statutory requirements, and project-specific environmental management measures.

Mandatory site briefing will be required. Meeting location is at Prince Edward Park Carpark off Prince Edward Park Rd Woronora NSW.

Background

The Mental Health Review Tribunal (known as the Tribunal or the MHRT) is an independent decision-making body under the Mental Health Act 2016 . The Tribunal is not part of any health service or treating team and its primary purpose is to review the involuntary status of persons with a mental illness and/or intellectual disability. The Tribunal also provides approval for the performance of electroconvulsive therapy and non-ablative neurosurgical procedures.

In making its decisions, the Tribunal must balance the rights of the consumer with the rights of others, including victims of unlawful acts, and the need to protect the community. Further, in exercising its jurisdiction, the Tribunal must act independently and is not subject to direction or control by any entity, including any Minister.

In undertaking the functions of the Tribunal, members require access to confidential information which is provided through the member only area of the MHRT website.

MHRT will require changes to the website, uploading of new documents and replacement of old ones. Support of the website is required. The requirement for maintenance is minimal after the security issues is resolved and would be on an as required basis.

Requirements

Experience with Webflow and Memberstack will be highly regarded.

Budget

Value of contract - $10,000 - $15,000. This budget includes the improved security for the member site and general maintenance on the website which will be on a needs basis.

regards

Fiona

4. Softfall (item 1.8): does Council prefer wetpour rubber, synthetic turf or organic mulch?

5. “Associated park infrastructure”: please confirm whether seats, a picnic setting, bins, an accessible path from the existing footpath, signage or a drinking fountain should be included.

6. Pump track (Option 2): is there a preferred target user group, surface (asphalt or compacted) or footprint?

7. Is any survey, services or geotechnical information available? Is a water connection available for irrigation?

8. What clearance and vehicle access must be kept for the sewer pump station?

9. Please advise the form of contract, retention and defects liability period that will apply.

Thanks
publicQuestions.answer:
1) Respondents capable of supplying both playground types are requested to provide pricing for both Option 1 and Option 2. Where a respondent can only provide one of the playground options, this should be clearly stated in the submission, and pricing should be provided for the applicable option.

2) Council's preferred shade solution is shade sails, as they provide an attractive and aesthetically appropriate outcome for a playground environment. Respondents should include a separate shade structure where required to provide adequate sun protection to key play areas, notwithstanding the integrated tower roofs included within the nominated play unit.

3) No playground or road-frontage fencing is required as part of this project. Fencing is only required around the transformer enclosures. Access gates to the transformer compounds shall have a minimum clear width of 1.5 metres, open outward, and include appropriate fence isolation and earthing provisions in accordance with Essential Energy requirements and applicable standards.

4) Council's preferred Softfall treatment is wet pour rubber.

5) The items listed above are not required and are not to be included within the scope of works at this stage of the playground development.

6) The intended primary users of the pump track are children aged up to 10 years. Preferred surface type is asphalt.

7) Available site services information is attached in “Site Plan with Service Lines”. A geotechnical investigation report may be made available where required. A water connection is available on site for irrigation purposes.

8) Vehicle access must be maintained around the perimeter of the sewer pump station boundary fence to allow for ongoing operational and maintenance requirements.

9) The contract will be administered as a lump sum contract. A Bank Guarantee equivalent to 10% of the contract value will be required as security. The Defects Liability Period (DLP) will be 12 months from the date of Practical Completion, during which the contractor will be responsible for rectifying any defects identified in the works.

Private patients:

Part B Schedule 1 clause 1.1(d) states that services should be available to both public and private patient cohorts, clause 3.5 Table 1 item 6 requires evidence of a Medicare provider number for each Medical Officer, and Attachment 3 Sections 2 and 3 seek private patient rates and an MBS fee. Evaluation weightings:

Hourly rate - clinician time:

(a) whether the hourly rate is intended to cover the Medical Officer’s non-patient-facing clinical time associated with each consultation, including pre-consultation review of referrals and results, documentation in the Eligible Customer’s clinical record, and the correspondence to the referring GP required under Part B Schedule 1 clause 1.4(c), or whether Suppliers may price that time separately; and

(b) whether charges are calculated per consultation (the hourly rate applied to the time allocated to consult) or on the Medical Officer’s rostered session time, including where a booked patient does not attend.

Hourly rate - service delivery costs:

Part B Schedule 2 clause 1.3 states that Prices are inclusive of all charges, expenses and overheads, and that obligations without a separate Price must be performed at no additional cost. Part C clause 7.1 asks Suppliers to detail any additional pricing or fees associated with the SOA, and Attachment 3, Section 2 includes a column for exclusions including cost. publicQuestions.question:
Council’s services spreadsheet omits a selectable Multidisciplinary Consultancy category although EOI identifies it. How should respondents nominate category G, and is a companion schedule acceptable?

May a respondent select a subcategory when only a defined structural engineering subset is offered, provided the limitations and specialist interfaces are disclosed in the methodology?

The evaluation criterion refers to category-specific publicly available standard and senior hourly rates, but the supplied workbook has only one pair of rate cells. Should respondents provide one pair overall or one pair per nominated category?

Are the EOI indicative hourly rates assessment-only, with future services priced through project-specific negotiated rates and lump-sum quotations, including travel and specialist disbursements?

How does Council assess regional/office-location contribution for a Melbourne-based specialist that regularly works in adjoining Byron Shire and will use approved local subcontractors?

Can respondents submit the names of intended specialists and state that ABN, formal consent and evidence will be provided if shortlisted, or must each prospective subconsultant be formally committed at EOI close?

For relevant-project value, will Council accept professional-service value as commercial-in-confidence (with a range or on-request disclosure), or is a numeric dollar figure mandatory?

Does Council require the entire Quality, Environmental and WHS management system manuals or are approved policies, plan summaries and sample registers sufficient? Is ISO accreditation optional?

For structural/temporary-works-only services under Roads and Traffic, must respondent hold a separate traffic-management/road safety accreditation, or is it acceptable for the traffic component to be separately subcontracted?

Are interstate engineers eligible for professional design roles subject to applicable NSW registration, and are there specific nominated disciplines/registration categories for this panel?

Are all seven categories intended to be accessible to small specialist firms, or will proposals be assessed against full-service requirements across each nominated category?

Can Council provide its Statement of Business Ethics and confirm acceptable method of signing the Conflict of Interest declaration (electronic signature or signed PDF)?

Will Council provide any standard panel deed, rate escalation provisions and interstate travel/disbursement policy before shortlisted respondents accept appointment?

Does Council intend to request specific local availability or maximum response times for emergency assessment call-outs, and may providers nominate advance mobilisation/lead times?
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1) Council’s services spreadsheet omits a selectable Multidisciplinary Consultancy category although EOI identifies it. How should respondents nominate category G, and is a companion schedule acceptable?

A1) Respondents can provide details of any multidisciplinary services as a separate submission.

Q2) May a respondent select a subcategory when only a defined structural engineering subset is offered, provided the limitations and specialist interfaces are disclosed in the methodology?

A2) Yes.

Q3) The evaluation criterion refers to category-specific publicly available standard and senior hourly rates, but the supplied workbook has only one pair of rate cells. Should respondents provide one pair overall or one pair per nominated category?

A3) Respondents should provide their highest senior and standard hourly rate for all, rather than each, categories. It will be considered as an indicative gauge of a respondents competitiveness.

Q4) Are the EOI indicative hourly rates assessment-only, with future services priced through project-specific negotiated rates and lump-sum quotations, including travel and specialist disbursements?

A4) Assessment only. Pricing will be requested and provided per separate RFQ's.

Q5) How does Council assess regional/office-location contribution for a Melbourne-based specialist that regularly works in adjoining Byron Shire and will use approved local subcontractors?

A5) Council will assess locality aspects from Local and Community criteria. It is suggested that any local sub-contractors are identified and location provided as part of Local and Community responses.

Q6) Can respondents submit the names of intended specialists and state that ABN, formal consent and evidence will be provided if shortlisted, or must each prospective subconsultant be formally committed at EOI close?

A6) It is suggested that a full list of possible sub-consultants be provided with their ABN.

Q7) For relevant-project value, will Council accept professional-service value as commercial-in-confidence (with a range or on-request disclosure), or is a numeric dollar figure mandatory?

A7) Respondents can provide a range of project value or provide no amount at all.

Q8) Does Council require the entire Quality, Environmental and WHS management system manuals or are approved policies, plan summaries and sample registers sufficient? Is ISO accreditation optional?

A8) Plan summaries are sufficient. Copies of accreditation would support any undertaking a respondent makes that they hold such accreditation.

Q9) For structural/temporary-works-only services under Roads and Traffic, must respondent hold a separate traffic-management/road safety accreditation, or is it acceptable for the traffic component to be separately subcontracted?

A9) Traffic compenents can be sub-contracted. Sun-contractors can be identified in the applicable requirement.

Q10) Are interstate engineers eligible for professional design roles subject to applicable NSW registration, and are there specific nominated disciplines/registration categories for this panel?

A10) Professional staff must hold valid registration in NSW for any services offered.

Q11) Are all seven categories intended to be accessible to small specialist firms, or will proposals be assessed against full-service requirements across each nominated category?

A11) Services for any sub-category can be offered.

Q12) Can Council provide its Statement of Business Ethics and confirm acceptable method of signing the Conflict of Interest declaration (electronic signature or signed PDF)?

A12) Councils Statement of Business ethics is available from Councils website via the link provided in the specifications. Electronic Signature of signed PDF are acceptable.

Q13) Will Council provide any standard panel deed, rate escalation provisions and interstate travel/disbursement policy before shortlisted respondents accept appointment?

A13) Council will issue an invited RFQ to applicable consultants from the shortlist which will include the scope/brief for works required on a case by case basis. The RFQ will specify the contract instrument and request fully itemised pricing.

Q14) Does Council intend to request specific local availability or maximum response times for emergency assessment call-outs, and may providers nominate advance mobilisation/lead times?

A14) Council will not specify or require any defined response times.

title: Long-Term Reliability and System Strength Services for the North Country
description:
Reliability and System Strength Services for the North Country (Long-Term) - WS5659204351

The Coordinator of Energy has determined, under clause 3.11A.4 of the Electricity System Market (ESM) Rules, to trigger a Non-Co-optimised Essential System Services (NCESS) procurement process by Western Power for Reliability and System Strength Services for the North Country.

The proposed services aim to address reliability and system strength concerns during planned or unplanned outage events affecting one or more 132 kV transmission lines supplying the North Country.

Call for NCESS Submissions

Western Power invites NCESS Submissions from prospective NCESS providers to deliver Reliability Services and/or System Strength Services located in the North Country. The North Country is defined as the area supplied by the Rangeway, Geraldton and Chapman substations.

This tender relates to the Long-Term contract term option (10-25 year terms). Proponents may offer a solution that fully or partially meets the requirements for either service (or both).

Activation requirements, performance measures, preferred connection locations and other technical requirements are set out in the Final NCESS Service Specification.

Queries may be submitted by email to emerging.technology.portfolio@westernpower.com.au or via the Q&A function in the VendorPanel portal.

Please submit NCESS Submissions via VendorPanel no later than 5:00pm (AWST) on 1 February 2027.

Interested NCESS providers should register with VendorPanel to be informed of whether any supporting documentation such as clarifications to questions may be published.

Council has received funding approval from the Australian Government under the Safer Local Roads and Infrastructure Program (the Program) to replace the existing timber bridge with a new concrete bridge with increased flood immunity. Delivering the day to day services for council is a professional and dynamic staff cohort of over 560 people including full time, contract and casual positions.

title: ITO - Network Hardware and Field Services
description: The procurement will establish a contemporary replacement arrangement to ensure continuity of network hardware supply, maintenance, support and lifecycle management across CITEC’s IP-VPN, Inter-Data Centre and Point-to-Point Optical Transport services. It will replace ageing infrastructure, introduce modern technologies and network management capabilities, and maintain a reliable, resilient and scalable network environment to meet CITEC and Queensland Government agency requirements over the next five to eight years, including supporting future agency participation.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:

Brisbane City, Queensland 4000
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: For over 50 years CITEC has provided technology infrastructure, business solutions and support to state government and commercial organisations nationwide.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Tuesday 27 October 2026 02:00 PM (E. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
The procurement has three key objectives:

•	End-of-life infrastructure by replacing ageing network assets with contemporary network components.

•	Enable future capability by implementing new technologies and network management capabilities that support CITEC and agency business requirements over the next five to eight years.

•	Maintain service continuity and supportability by ensuring appropriate levels of hardware, software, support and maintenance capability are maintained throughout the network lifecycle.

Through this procurement, CITEC will establish the contractual arrangements necessary to maintain a resilient, supported and scalable network environment for existing customers, while providing the flexibility and capacity to support additional Queensland Government agencies seeking access to CITEC network services.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
This Invitation to Offer (ITO) is divided into four parts, reflecting the key categories of network infrastructure, equipment and associated services required by CITEC. Suppliers may submit a tender for any single part, multiple parts, or all four parts, in any combination.

•	Part A – Network Hardware, Support and Associated Services: Covers the supply of network hardware and associated manufacturer support, maintenance and lifecycle services required to support CITEC’s existing and future network environments.

•	Part B – Optical Network Infrastructure and Services: Covers optical network requirements, including the supply of optical equipment and associated technology, together with technical support and field services. This part is intended to support current requirements and future optical network availability, capacity and capability.

•	Part C – Break-Fix Replacement Services: Covers the supply and replacement of network equipment and components required to respond to break-fix incidents and restore network services. This includes the provision of replacement equipment and associated services necessary to maintain service continuity and operational availability.

•	Part D – Other Network Equipment and Services: Covers future capability and other equipment, technologies and associated services that may be required by CITEC from time to time, including equipment and capabilities such as virtual laboratory environments, firewalls and other network or technology solutions that fall outside the specific scope of Parts A, B and C.

The four parts are intended to provide CITEC with flexible contract arrangements that can accommodate current operational requirements while supporting future technology replacement, network expansion, service continuity and emerging technology needs. Suppliers may tender for one or more parts based on their capabilities and areas of expertise.

publicQuestions.answer:
PLEASE FIND ANSWERS BENEATH EACH QUESTION BELOW:

o Will CITEC appoint more than one supplier for the same OEM? The ITO states that CITEC may award to one or more suppliers for each Part.

It is possible; however, it is more likely there will be one supplier per OEM. There may be instances where a supplier is a preferred supplier for a particular OEM, however that supplier also has relationships with other OEMs.

o If multiple suppliers are appointed to a Part, can CITEC please clarify the intended operating model for the resulting arrangement, including how requirements and purchase orders will be allocated between successful suppliers? For example, will suppliers be ranked or categorised, will individual requirements be subject to secondary quotation/competition, or will CITEC have discretion to procure directly from any appointed supplier?

If multiple suppliers are appointed to a Part, it is more likely that the part is broken up and those suppliers will exclusively provide the part they are appointed to. o The workbook refers to "Appendix X v0.47", but the spec we were given is Appendix 1.

Section 2.4.2.7 directs respondents to include all components within a single line response in the equipment package workbooks. How should the full list of components be presented given we are not permitted to add or modify rows or sheets? Can CITEC please advise how they would like this information presented to ensure transparency of included equipment? Is a supplementary document with full BOM breakdown suitable)?

For each hardware line item listed within the QG-CDSB-2026-212 – Product Capability Spreadsheet, if there is an additional cost for an ‘associated required component’ that is not presently listed out in a separate line, that ‘associated required component’ pricing must be included with the Hardware pricing, and a notation of this should be made in ‘Respondent Notes’.

SFP quantities on the equipment package sheets do not seem consistent with the diagrams provided or the expected connectivity required (e.g. LAN-M-1B has 4 L2 switches with 8 SFPs, 1 L3 switches with 5 SFPs. Can CITEC please validate and confirm the quantities of SFPs required per package in the spreadsheet?

Where a discrepancy exists between Appendix 1 – Functional And Technical Specifications and QG-CDSB-2026-212 – Product Capability Spreadsheet, always select QG-CDSB-2026-212 – Product Capability Spreadsheet as the source of truth.

It is noted that the package name is for a pack of 10 access points, but the formulas assume this price should be multiplied by 10. This will result in 100 APs rather than 10. Can CITEC please confirm whether unit price is intended to be per AP, or per pack of 10 APs.

Please provide pricing for 10 Access Points, CITEC will not multiply on this line.

Please confirm that references to trunk ports and interconnect ports (e.g. 10Gbps trunk port to Layer-three switches) refers to uplink ports in the switch Can CITEC please confirm this is the intended interpretation of trunk ports and interconnect ports

Trunk port refers to the function of carrying multiple vlans across an uplink from a switch to another switch or router. Interconnect port refers to a port on the switch to switch to form one logical switch (switch stack)

Please confirm whether each part must be bid in it's entirety, or will partial bid be accepted for separate modules (e.g. in Part D) Can CITEC please confirm that it is acceptable to quote on individual modules in Part D without responding to the entire Part D?

You are able to respond to sections of Part D and do not have to respond to the whole of Part D.

Reference to lifecycle stage is slightly ambiguous Can CITEC please clarify whether the lifecycle stage referred to on page 6 refers to the current age of infrastructure (hence switches would be replaced first, in about 3 years’ time), or the projected refresh scope (in which routers would be replaced first, in year 1)?

The lifecycle stage refers to the current age of infrastructure.

There is no clear section of the pricing workbook where cross-functional services (such as service delivery management or client experience management) should be quoted. Can CITEC please advise how they would like cross-functional and service management costs represented?

These items could be quoted within the ‘Innovation’ tab within the QG-CDSB-2026-212 – Product Capability Spreadsheet

title: 201222 Minor Works Construction Panel
description:
Council is seeking to establish a panel of suitably qualified contractors to deliver minor construction, refurbishment, repair, installation and associated trade services across its owned and managed assets.

The panel will provide a flexible and efficient procurement mechanism for engaging pre-qualified suppliers to undertake minor works activities valued at up to $250,000 (including GST) per engagement. Services may be required across a diverse range of Council facilities and infrastructure, including community buildings, sporting and recreational facilities, parks, depots, commercial properties, heritage assets and public amenities. Contractors will be required to provide all labour, materials, plant, equipment, supervision, permits and associated resources necessary to complete assigned works.

This panel will support Council asset management, service delivery and capital works objectives by ensuring timely access to capable contractors, improving procurement efficiency, reducing project delivery timeframes and maintaining the safety, functionality and value of Council assets.

This panel contract is intended for the delivery of minor construction works with an individual project, work order, quotation or engagement value not exceeding $250,000 (including GST). Council reserves the right to determine the suitability of works for procurement through this panel and may elect to undertake separate procurement processes for projects exceeding this threshold.

publicQuestions.answer:

1. The submitted Schedule of Rates will establish the maximum rates applicable under the panel. Contractors may provide project-specific quotations, including lump sum pricing, to reflect the scope, complexity, site conditions and delivery requirements of individual works packages; however, any pricing derived from the Schedule of Rates must not exceed the applicable tendered rates. Contractors may quote rates lower than those submitted where appropriate for a particular engagement.

2. Tenderers nominating multiple service categories will be assessed separately against each category nominated. Appointment to the panel will be determined on a category-by-category basis, and a tenderer may therefore be successful in one or more nominated categories without necessarily being appointed to all categories for which they have submitted.

3. Emergency response requirements will be determined on a project-by-project basis and may vary depending on the nature, complexity and scope of the works, site conditions, operational requirements and the urgency of the situation. Any specific response time requirements will be communicated as part of the individual engagement. After-hours works will be considered based on the hours of work and availability submitted by each tenderer as part of their tender response, together with the requirements of the individual engagement.

title: Remove and Replace Roof Structures, Opal Street WTP Filters
description:
Central Highlands Regional Council operates the Opal Street Water Treatment Plant (WTP) located in Emerald, Queensland. The WTP incorporates four rapid gravity sand filters which form a critical component of the potable water treatment process.

Each filter is currently protected by an individual structural steel roof structure. Over time, these roof structures have deteriorated and are approaching the end of their serviceable life. In addition to their deteriorated condition, the existing roof structures do not adequately facilitate the operational requirements associated with periodic filter media replacement.

During future filter media replacement campaigns, one-tonne bulk sandbags are required to be lowered into the filter compartments via crane. The existing roof structures do not provide suitable openings through which these bags can be safely lowered into the filters. This creates operational difficulties and increases risk during maintenance activities.

Central Highlands Regional Council is seeking responses from suitably qualified and experienced contractors to undertake the design, removal, disposal, supply and construction of replacement roof structures over the four rapid gravity filters.

The replacement roof structures must incorporate suitable access openings that facilitate the future lowering of one-tonne bulk bags of filter media into each filter compartment by others under a separate contract.

The Works are to be delivered under a Design and Construct Contract.

The Contractor must provide all labour, design services, engineering services, supervision, plant, equipment, materials, transport, certifications and incidentals required to complete the Works.

The Works include, but are not limited to:

• Site inspection and verification of existing conditions.

• Detailed design of replacement roof structures for four rapid gravity sand filters.

• Structural design certification by a Registered Professional Engineer of Queensland (RPEQ).

• Preparation and submission of design documentation and drawings.

• Attendance at, facilitation of and incorporation of feedback from an 80% design review workshop with Central Highlands Regional Council Water Utilities personnel. The Contractor must present theproposed design, demonstrate how operational requirements have been addressed, and provide draft design documentation for review prior to finalisation of the design.

• Removal and lawful disposal of existing roof structures. This includes the temporary covering of the sand filter opening to avoid any contaminants entering the filter media.

• Supply and installation of new roof structures.

• Provision of access openings to facilitate future filter media replacement activities.

• Supply and installation of all structural steelwork, roofing, flashings, lighting, stormwater runoff piping to prevent filter contamination, fixings and protective coatings.

• Final inspection and commissioning.

• Provision of as-constructed drawings and documentation.

• Handover of the completed Works.

The Contractor must be responsible for delivering a complete and fit-for-purpose solution.

Prior to commencing work on site, the Contractor must prepare, submit, revise and implement project-specific management plans suitable for the Works, including safety/WHS, environmental, quality, demolition, construction methodology/site management and traffic/pedestrian/access management plans, as applicable.

The replacement of filter media is specifically excluded from this Contract and will be undertaken by others under a separate contract.

Where the Opal St WTP Filter Media Replacement technical specification prepared by AECOM is provided with this RFT, only Sections 3.0 Materials and Construction, 4.0 Design and Documentation and 5.0 Roof Structure Removal and Reinstatement apply to this Contract, and only to the extent relevant to the design, removal, disposal, supply and construction of replacement roof structures. All other sections of that document are provided for information only unless expressly referenced in this Specification. In the event of inconsistency, this Specification takes precedence.

The Contractor must supply all labour, supervision, engineering services, design services, plant, equipment, materials, transport, temporary works and incidentals necessary to complete the Works.

The Works must be undertaken at the Opal Street Water Treatment Plant, Opal Street, Emerald, Queensland.

The Contract will commence within 7 days after the Award Letter and Contractual Arrangement are provided to and signed by the successful Contractor. Central Highlands Regional Council anticipates the contract end date to be as per the approved contract schedule.

publicQuestions.question:
Good day,

Thanks for the Site visit.

Can you clearly define the Battery limits on the Existing concrete structure.

The RFT says the contractor’s design must include verification of the existing support structures, foundations, dimensions, levels, interfaces and affected services.

This as stated is no small task and I am unsure of the intent. Due to the level of movement of the structure that was noted and commented on by CHRC rep it is evident that the current foundations have had issues. Further to this The AECOM specification is relevant here because it actually contains a dedicated “Concrete Rehabilitation” section, covering concrete breakout/removal, exposed reinforcement treatment, substrate preparation, repair materials, reinstatement, finishing, curing, inspection and testing. So I need to understand a clear battery limit.

The design requirements also explicitly say the new roof design must “include lighting and rainwater disposal.”

Can you please provide the Design or Design intent for both of these items. Where is the power coming from? Has the engineering been completed? What lights do you require and where? How many of them? Where is the rain water to go? What are the tie in points? Sorry but the CHRC Rep was not aware of any of the details.

The CHRC Rep was of the understanding that these roof structures were to fully enclose the WTP filters down and sealed onto the concrete, completely sealed from wind and rain water, also vermin proff. Please confirm this is the intent that a fully sealed area is required not just replacement roof structures.

Can you confirm the expected shutdown/staging arrangement? Can only one complete filter pair/two cells be taken offline at a time, and must each filter be completely returned to service before the next roof is removed?

What is the maximum allowable outage for each filter? Is there a preferred low-demand period or particular months when Council wants construction undertaken?

Are there existing structural drawings for all four filter concrete structures? We understand the filters were built at different times and may not be identical.

Does Council have a preferred new roof arrangement? Skillion, gable, similar to existing, or is the geometry entirely contractor-designed?

What corrosion protection system does Council expect for the structural steel? Is hot-dip galvanising acceptable/preferred, or is a duplex/coating system required? The new design has a minimum 25-year service-life requirement.

Please clarify exactly how Council expects the two access openings per filter to operate. Must operators be able to physically open them without mechanical lifting equipment, or is crane removal of a roof cassette acceptable?

Is the specified minimum 2 m × 2 m clear opening required for each individual filter cell without exception?

How does Council envisage the one-tonne bulk bags being lowered through the roof? What crane/telehandler will normally be used, and from which side of each filter?

If removable roof sections are acceptable, does Council require permanent certified lifting points and a documented lifting procedure?

What permanent working-at-heights system is expected? Static line, fall-arrest anchors, ladder attachment points, roof access walkway, or simply engineered attachment provisions?

What temporary protection is required over the open filters during demolition and construction? Does Council require a rigid engineered cover, sealed membrane system, or another defined standard?

Can a reusable temporary filter cover be moved progressively from Filter 1 to Filter 4, or does Council require multiple covers to be available simultaneously?

Are there contamination-control requirements beyond physically covering the filter? For example restrictions on grinding, hot work, galvanised material handling, drilling, dust generation or chemicals near an operating filter.

Can we perform hot works above/adjacent to the filters once an approved temporary cover is fitted? Or does Council expect essentially all cutting/welding to be completed off site?

Where can cranes be positioned for each of the four filters? We need to establish available radius and likely crane capacity.

Are there known underground services beneath the proposed crane/outrigger locations? Can Council supply service plans?

Does Council have information on pavement/ground bearing capacity for crane outriggers? If not, what verification will be required?

Who performs plant isolations — Council operators or AMM? What notice period is required?

Is condensation underneath the roof currently an issue? Does Council expect insulation or anti-condensation roof backing?

title: W4Q Community Halls Renewal Project – Principal Contractor
description:
Central Highlands Regional Council has secured funding through the Works for Queensland (W4Q)

Program to undertake renewal and functionality improvements across selected community halls within

the Central Highlands Region.

The project seeks to improve accessibility, community participation, presentation capability, hearing

augmentation, lighting performance and supporting infrastructure while ensuring compliance with

applicable funding requirements.

The Contractor shall provide a complete Design and Construct solution including:

• Site validation

• Design development

• Procurement

• Installation

• Testing

• Commissioning

• Training

• Handover

• Warranty support

The completed works shall be fully operational at Practical Completion.

Mandatory Requirements

Failure to meet any mandatory requirement may result in the quotation being

excluded from evaluation.

The Tenderer must:

• Hold a current ABN

• Hold all required licences and registrations

• Hold a current Queensland Electrical Contractor Licence

• Maintain Workers Compensation Insurance

• Maintain Public Liability Insurance ($20M minimum)

• Maintain Professional Indemnity Insurance ($5M minimum)

• Maintain Contract Works Insurance

• Demonstrate relevant experience in similar projects

• Comply with Queensland WHS and Electrical Safety legislation

• Accept the Conditions of Contract

• Demonstrate capacity to complete the Works

A9. SITE VALIDATION REQUIREMENTS

Prior to commencing design development, the Contractor shall undertake

comprehensive site validation.

Site validation shall include:

• Existing dimensions

• Existing electrical infrastructure

• Existing switchboards

• Existing lighting systems

• Existing accessibility provisions

• Existing building condition

• Existing AV infrastructure

• Existing services

• Existing site constraints

Any discrepancy identified during site validation shall be reported to Council.

The Contractor shall not rely upon reference drawings or photographs for

final installation purposes.

A10. DESIGN DEVELOPMENT REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall undertake all design development required to deliver the

required performance outcomes.

Design development shall include:

• Design markups

• Shop drawings

• Equipment schedules

• Installation layouts

• Commissioning plans

Project Objectives

The objectives of the project are:

• Improve accessibility and community inclusion

• Improve community usability and functionality

• Improve hearing accessibility and presentation capability

• Improve lighting quality, reliability and energy efficiency

• Validate and improve electrical infrastructure supporting the Works

• Improve the condition and functionality of community facilities

• Deliver a practical and sustainable outcome within available funding

• Maximise community benefit from the approved W4Q funding allocation

A1. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall:

• Validate all existing conditions

• Verify all dimensions

• Verify existing electrical infrastructure

• Verify existing services

• Verify accessibility conditions

• Verify installation locations

• Verify compliance obligations

Reference drawings, photographs, sketches and markups supplied by

Council are indicative only and shall not relieve the Contractor of

responsibility for site verification.

• Cable pathways

• Equipment mounting details

• Accessibility details

The Contractor shall provide all information necessary to demonstrate

compliance with project objectives and funding requirements.

A11. ELECTRICAL PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall:

• Validate earthing systems

• Validate switchboards

• Validate circuit protection

• Validate circuit capacity

• Validate electrical infrastructure supporting the works

• Undertake targeted rectification required to support approved W4Q

outcomes

Any additional compliance issues, asset renewal requirements or remediation

works not required to support the approved scope shall be separately

identified and priced.

All electrical works shall comply with:

• AS/NZS 3000

• Queensland Electrical Safety legislation

• Relevant Australian Standards

• Manufacturer requirements

A13. LIGHTING PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall provide energy-efficient LED lighting suitable for

community hall use.

Lighting systems shall:

• Improve energy efficiency

• Improve reliability

• Improve maintainability

• Improve functionality

• Improve user comfort

• Provide suitable illumination levels

The Contractor shall ensure lighting solutions are appropriate to each facility

and intended community use.

A12. PRESENTATION SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS

Where presentation systems are installed, they shall provide:

• Simple operation

• Reliable functionality

• Suitability for community meetings

• Suitability for civic events

• Suitability for training sessions

• Suitability for presentations

• Ease of maintenance

Presentation systems may include:

• Displays

• Mounting systems

• Input connectivity

• Audio integration

• User controls

The Contractor shall provide user training and operating instructions.

A13. ACCESSIBILITY REQUIREMENTS

Accessibility improvements shall:

• Improve community access

• Improve facility usability

• Improve community participation

• Support inclusive use of facilities

• Comply with applicable standards

Accessibility works may include:

• Handrails

• Door improvements

• Pathway improvements

• Entry modifications

• Amenity improvements

• Hearing augmentation

• Accessibility signage

A14. QUALITY MANAGEMENT REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall maintain an appropriate Quality Management System.

The Contractor shall prepare and maintain:

• Inspection and Test Plans

• Defects Register

• Non-Conformance Register

• Commissioning Records

• Quality Assurance Records

Council may request evidence of quality controls at any time.

A15. ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall:

• Control dust

• Control noise

• Control waste

• Minimise environmental impacts

• Remove waste from site

• Comply with environmental legislation

The Contractor shall leave all facilities in a clean and operational condition.

A16. WORK HEALTH AND SAFETY REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall prepare and implement:

• WHS Management Plan

• Safe Work Method Statements

• Site Inductions

• Emergency Procedures

• Incident Reporting Procedures

• All works shall comply with Queensland WHS legislation

A19. REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

Weekly Reports shall include:

• Progress achieved

• Planned activities

• Safety performance

• Risks

• Procurement status

• Variations

• Issues requiring Council attention

Monthly Reports shall include:

• Program status

• Cost status

• Forecast completion

• Key risk

• Outstanding actions

• Funding status

• Scope status

A17. WARRANTIES

The Contractor shall provide a Warranty Register at Practical Completion

detailing all warranties provided under the Contract.

A24. W4Q FUNDING COMPLIANCE

The Contractor shall ensure all proposed solutions remain compliant with

Works for Queensland funding requirements.

The Contractor shall immediately notify Council if any proposed solution may:

• Impact funding eligibility

• Expand scope beyond approved objectives

• Introduce theatre infrastructure

• Introduce entertainment infrastructure

• Introduce ICT modernisation

• Introduce network modernisation

• Create grant compliance risk

• No such work shall proceed without written approval from Council.
